chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdul Karim ibn Amr, from Abdul A'la, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: A man pelts the Jamarah with six pebbles, and one falls among the (other) pebbles. He said: He should repeat it, if he so desires, from that moment, and if he so desires, from the next day when he intends the pelting; and he should not take from the pebbles of the Jamarah.
He said: And I asked him about a man who pelts Jamarat al-Aqabah with six pebbles, and one falls in the carriage. He said: He should repeat it.

key_terms.الْجَمْرَة: The stone pillar or site where pebbles are cast during Hajj
key_terms.الْمَحْمِل: Carriage or load, here referring to the container or pile holding the pebbles
key_terms.جَمْرَة الْعَقَبَة: The specific Jamarah (pillar) in Mina, typically the first one stoned

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pebble falls among others during the stoning of Jamarah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of Hajj rituals, specifically addressing the validity of the stoning (Ramy) when a pebble is lost or falls into the carrier (Mahmal). It establishes that the pilgrim must replace the missed pebble, offering flexibility to do so immediately or the following day before the next casting, while emphasizing that the replacement is drawn from the general pile rather than the specific set already used. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the completeness of ritual actions while accommodating practical difficulties during the pilgrimage.
